parameters.name: zone-name

host-inbound-traffic system-services all.explanation: The command `host-inbound-traffic system-services [parameter3]` allows specified system services (e.g., SSH, SNMP) to receive traffic on the device's management interface.

parameters.name: system-services
parameters.explanation: Allowed type of system service, e.g. all system services.

set security zones security-zone untrust.explanation: This command fragment configures a security zone named `[parameter1]` within the Junos security zones hierarchy, defining a logical boundary for security policies and interfaces.

parameters.name: zone-name

parameters.explanation: Allowed type of system service, e.g. all system services.

set security policies from-zone trust.explanation: The command sets the source zone for a security policy in Junos OS, defining the network area from which traffic originates, with `[parameter1]` specifying the zone name.

parameters.name: from-zone
parameters.explanation: Source security area name, such as trust.

to-zone untrust.explanation: The command `to-zone [parameter2]` specifies the destination security zone in a Junos security policy, defining where traffic is allowed to flow.

parameters.name: to-zone
parameters.explanation: Purpose security area name, e.g. untrust.

policy permit-all.explanation: The command `policy [parameter3]` in Junos defines or references a routing policy named `[parameter3]` to control route advertisement or acceptance.

parameters.name: policy
parameters.explanation: Policy name, for example, permit-all.

match source-address any.explanation: The command fragment `match source-address [parameter4]` filters traffic based on the specified source IP address (`[parameter4]`) in a Junos firewall or policy configuration.

parameters.name: source-address
parameters.explanation: Source address matches, e.g. Any indicates any address.

match destination-address any.explanation: The command fragment `match destination-address [parameter4]` filters traffic based on the specified destination IP address or address range in a Junos policy or firewall rule.

parameters.name: destination-address
parameters.explanation: Destination address matches, e.g. Any indicates any address.

match application any.explanation: The command `match application [parameter4]` filters traffic based on the specified application (parameter4) in a Junos firewall or security policy.

parameters.name: application
parameters.explanation: Apply matching conditions, e.g. Any indicates arbitrary application.

then permit.explanation: The `then [parameter4]` command in Junos specifies the action to take in a firewall filter or policy, such as `accept`, `discard`, or `reject`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.explanation: Process actions that match traffic, such as permit, are allowed through.

set security nat source rule-set rs1.explanation: This command configures a source NAT rule set in Junos, defining a collection of rules for translating source IP addresses in traffic matching specified criteria.

parameters.name: rule-set-name
parameters.explanation: Name of the NAT rule book.

from zone trust.explanation: Configure the source safety area for the NAT ruleset application.

parameters.name: zone
parameters.explanation: Name of the source security area.

to zone untrust.explanation: Configure the purpose safe area for the NAT ruleset application.

parameters.name: zone
parameters.explanation: The name of the destination security area.

rule r1.explanation: The command `rule [parameter2]` in Junos defines a specific rule within a firewall filter or policy, where `[parameter2]` specifies the rule's name or identifier.

parameters.name: rule
parameters.explanation: NAT rule name, e.g. r1.

match source-address 192.168.10.0/24.explanation: The command `match source-address [parameter3]` filters traffic based on the specified source IP address or address range in a Junos policy or firewall rule.

parameters.name: source-address
parameters.explanation: Source address matching conditions, e.g. 192.168.100.0/24.

then source-nat interface.explanation: The command `then source-nat [parameter3]` in Junos applies source network address translation (NAT) using the specified NAT pool or interface defined in `[parameter3]`.

parameters.name: source-nat
parameters.explanation: NAT action type, e.g. interface for interface NAT.

set security nat static rule-set static-.explanation: This command fragment configures a static NAT rule-set in Junos, defining a set of rules for translating private IP addresses to public IP addresses.

parameters.name: rule-set-name
parameters.explanation: The name of the static NAT ruleset.

from zone untrust.explanation: The command fragment `from zone [parameter2]` specifies the source zone in a Junos security policy, defining the traffic origin for policy evaluation.

parameters.name: from-zone
parameters.explanation: Source area name, e.g. untrust.

rule static-nat1.explanation: The command `rule [parameter2]` in Junos defines a specific rule within a firewall filter or policy, where `[parameter2]` specifies the rule's name or identifier.

parameters.name: rule
parameters.explanation: Static NAT rules name, e.g., status-nat1.

match destination-address 1.1.1.100/32.explanation: The command fragment `match destination-address [parameter3]` filters traffic based on the specified destination IP address or address range in a Junos policy or firewall rule.

parameters.name: destination-address
parameters.explanation: Purpose address matching conditions, such as 1.1.1.100/32.

then static-nat prefix 192.168.10.10/32.explanation: The command configures static NAT by mapping a specified source IP prefix (`[parameter3]`) to a predefined destination IP address or range.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.explanation: Static NAT prefixes, e.g. 192.168.10.10/32.

set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0.explanation: This command configures an OSPF area in Junos OS, where `[parameter1]` specifies the area ID, enabling OSPF routing within the defined area.

parameters.name: area
parameters.explanation: OSPF area ID.

interface ge-0/0/1.0.explanation: Configure interfaces in the OSPF area.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: Interface name, e.g., g-1/0/0.0.

set routing-options static route 0.0.0.0.explanation: This command configures a static route in the routing table, where `[parameter1]` specifies the destination network prefix and its next-hop or discard/ reject behavior.

parameters.name: route
parameters.explanation: Target network address.

next-hop 2.2.2.2.explanation: This command configures a static route in Junos, where `[parameter1]` is the destination network and `[parameter2]` specifies the next-hop IP address for forwarding traffic.

parameters.name: next-hop
parameters.explanation: Next jump address.
